architectural_layer: existing local PR identity owner, provider read adapter and submission/prospective consumers
operation_side: authenticated query before qualification or mutation
invariant: An authenticated bound PR supplies its exact base/head relationship; default branch is not a substitute for that relationship. Candidate-local proof never grants provider certification, protected-main or release authority.
contract: Extend the existing LocalPRContext owner rather than introduce a second base resolver, CLI intent flag or semantic registry. Preserve legacy unbound context serialization and existing public CLI grammar.

Distinguish repository default branch, PR base branch and exact comparison SHA, provider-observed head and current local candidate. Newly authored descendants are not silently identical to an already observed provider head.

Authenticate provider repository identity against the selected remote and complete open PR inventory; exactly one branch/repository match binds a PR. Duplicate, malformed, moved, wrong repository, wrong ref or unavailable bound facts reject before generation/proof/effects. Absence must be authenticated; provider errors never become an empty inventory.

Fetch and verify exact referenced Git objects and ancestry through the existing bounded immutable Git read owner. Preserve default-branch behavior for authenticated unbound and genuinely local non-provider repositories; unprovable GitHub identity cannot confer submit authority.

Propagate the same comparison context to source checks, changelog, planning, local synthetic PR event, prospective proof, exact push, existing PR projection and late unchanged checks. A provider/local head advancement requires an explicit same-branch descendant transition and reauthentication at its consuming boundary.

Preserve separate authority contexts: a feature-branch PR base does not grant protected-default-main, bounded/phase, controller or release authority. Existing repository protection and finalizer/evaluator owners retain their propositions. No force-push, blind retry or mutation inference.

Existing PR reuse binds actual base ref/SHA rather than requiring every PR base equal repository default. Creation of an unbound PR continues to derive the default target. Protected merge requests remain independently gated by the actual target protection contract.

All existing concrete success/error serialization must remain compatible in unchanged unbound contexts. Changes to previously rejected or unprovable states are additive safety behavior; any unavoidable valid public contract break blocks activation pending explicit migration/version decision.
Remain isolated from live canonical attempt 5. Do not merge or activate an incomplete subset that changes local base while leaving consumers on default-branch assumptions.
